abstract: The scarcity of human-annotated literary corpora limits the development of domain-specific sentiment analysis models. This study investigates whether LLM-generated annotations can supervise smaller models for literary sentiment analysis. We fine-tune five BERT models using ordinal regression on 10,889 literary sentences annotated by Gemma 4 31B on a ten-point sentiment scale. The models are evaluated against 1,923 human-annotated sentences from Hemingway's "The Old Man and the Sea", alongside the teacher model and conventional baselines. BERT-large achieves a Kendall's $\tau$ of 0.589, approaching the teacher's 0.604. Although a constant-neutral predictor achieves the lowest overall mean absolute error (MAE), BERT-base outperforms the teacher on non-neutral sentences, achieving an MAE of 0.726 versus 1.116. These findings demonstrate the potential of LLM-generated supervision for developing smaller literary sentiment models, while highlighting the limitations of aggregate error metrics on predominantly neutral datasets.
abstract_zh: 人类注释的文学语料库稀缺限制了特定领域情感分析模型的发展。本研究探讨了大型语言模型（LLM）生成的注释是否可以监督较小的模型进行文学情感分析。我们对使用Gemma 4 31B在十点情感评分上标注的10,889个文学句子进行了五个BERT模型的序数回归微调。模型的评估基于来自海明威《老人与海》的1,923个人工标注句子，以及教师模型和传统基线。BERT-large的Kendall's τ为0.589，接近教师模型的0.604。尽管常数中性预测器的总体平均绝对误差（MAE）最低，但BERT-base在非中性句子上的表现优于教师模型，MAE为0.726，而教师模型为1.116。这些发现展示了LLM生成的监督在开发较小的文学情感模型中的潜力，同时突显了在以中性数据集为主的情况下，聚合误差指标的局限性。
title: Distilling Literary Sentiment from LLM Annotations into an Ordinal BERT Model
title_zh: 从大型语言模型注释中提炼文学情感至序数BERT模型
